summary: Kings County lookout on the Kettleman Hills North Dome, run by the West Side fire district 1935-1937; FFLOS lists it Gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.agency: West Side Fire Protection District of Kings County
facts.status_note: Listed Gone by the Forest Lookout Association; the sources give no year or cause for removal

events.note: Mr. and Mrs. O.H. Upton of Hanford to be on duty around the clock at the station
Telephone installed at the station by June 1935, reached through the Coalinga exchange
Guy Knapp in charge at the station during fire hazard season; station to open May 5
Guy Knapp in charge again; station to open May 5; no truck at the site, fires phoned to Cottonwood Pass and Kettleman City

evidence.supports: West Side district of Kings County to have two stations in operation the next day, Point Lacima one of them (notice of May 29, 1935)
evidence.quote: The recently organized West Side Fire Protection District of Kings County will have two fire lookout stations in operation tomorrow

evidence.supports: Station to be linked by telephone via the Avenal and Coalinga lines through oil companies (1935)
evidence.quote: A station at Point Lacima on the Kettleman Hills Skyline Boulevard will be connected by telephone with the Avenal and Coalinga lines through an arrangement made with various oil companies.

evidence.supports: Upton couple of Hanford to be on duty around the clock (1935)
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. O.H. Upton of Hanford will be on duty, giving twenty-four hour service.

evidence.supports: Telephone installed, reached through the Coalinga exchange (June 1935)
evidence.quote: A telephone has been installed in the Point Lacima lookout station on the Kettleman Hills north dome and may be reached through the Coalinga exchange

evidence.supports: Station to open May 5, 1936, on the North Dome
evidence.quote: The Point Lacima fire lookout station on the North Dome of Kettleman Hills will open May 5

evidence.supports: County fire warden J.C. Griswold announced the May 5 opening (April 29, 1936)
evidence.quote: The Point Lacima fire lookout station on the North Dome of Kettleman Hills will open May 5, it was announced today by J.C. Griswold, who, as county fire warden, is in charge of the fire protection activities

evidence.supports: Guy Knapp in charge during fire hazard season (1936)
evidence.quote: Guy Knapp will be in charge at the lookout station during fire hazard season.
On Point Lacima, location of the lookout station on the North Dome of the Kettleman Hills, Guy Knapp will be in charge.

evidence.supports: No truck at the site; fires phoned to Cottonwood Pass and Kettleman City (1937)
evidence.quote: There will be no truck at this location, but the lookout will telephone locations of fires to the Cottonwood Pass and Kettleman City stations.

evidence.supports: Listed as Kings County, type Unknown, status Gone
Kettleman Hills are the location of the Kettleman North Dome Oil Field
evidence.quote: They are the location of the Kettleman North Dome Oil Field

evidence.supports: Oil field occupies the northernmost portion of the Kettleman Hills
evidence.quote: The Kettleman North Dome occupies the northernmost portion of the Kettleman Hills

notes_for_editor: No build date or design found in the sources read. The 1935-37 notices come from newspapers quoted on Forest Lookouts; the 1937 notice says the station 'will open' May 5, so the opening is not confirmed. The brief's coordinates (36.00395, -120.0571) match FFLOS; the Wikipedia Kettleman Hills infobox gives a close point. FFLOS type is Unknown and the brief kind agrees, so no correction. Not tried: Hanford Sentinel or Fresno Bee archives after 1937, which might show when the station closed. Budget: 2 searches, 4 page reads.
